routes.reason: Source of BunGAndNewtonStrata BG2–BG3 for the only two missing items: Theorem 2.7.3, the Newton stratification of the flag variety recalled from [CS17, §3], and the ordinary stratum. The route is right and its reason is the useful part — BG2–BG3 own |Bun_G| → B(G), the semicontinuity of ν and the Newton strata, while IG.3–IG.7 use 'flag Newton strata' without constructing them, so this is a real hole in the atlas's supply chain rather than a formality. BunGAndNewtonStrata is campaign-origin and both stages exist.

notes: Accept. 70 items, 68 planned and 2 missing, the missing pair routed once. The unusual distribution is correct and not a sign of over-claiming: IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration ('Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration') was designed from this paper — its layer descriptions cite 'CSnc §2.1' and the paper's own constructions by name — so 55 of the 68 planned items land in the roadmap built for them, and the rest go to PELModuli, ShimuraCompactifications, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties, EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison and the étale-cohomology layers that own their subject. All 35 distinct planned layer ids exist in data/atlas.json. I reproduced the recorded hash of arXiv v2 (803fc16a…), the accepted version the extraction read. The locators hold: of the 92 checks, 89 land on exactly the page given and the other three are parts of a theorem or steps of a proof that run onto the next page (Theorem 2.5.9's part (4) on p. 28, Theorem 6.4.1's proof on pp. 85 and 87), each confirmed by reading. All twelve findings are printed exactly as quoted, and several are checkable beyond the quotation: E2 and E3 form a coherent pair, since §2.5.4 on p. 26 derives 'inclusions M_{Z′} ⊂ M_Z' from its hypothesis while Theorem 2.5.9(4) on p. 28 prints 'via the inclusion M_Z ⊆ M_{Z′}' — the two passages contradict each other, and the corrections make them agree; E12's 'Proposition 2.8.4 and Corollary 2.8.2' is refuted by the labels' own occurrences on pp. 34 and 36, which are Lemma 2.8.4 and Proposition 2.8.2; and E8 I checked in the published [CS17] itself (Annals 186 (2017), fetched from the Annals site), where 5.5.3 is a Remark and Theorem 5.5.4 is the Galois-representation statement, exactly as the finding says. E6's argument is sound: as printed g ↦ g^♯ would reverse products, so θ could not act by a group automorphism. Nothing was corrected, rejected or deleted.
